complexity.notes: Correct but uses O(n) extra space for the array; your previous submission solved the same problem in O(1) space by reversing the pointers in place, which is the approach interviewers usually expect here. The loop is a bit indirect: it appends a trailing None purely so `nodes[i-1]` reads None at i=0 via negative indexing — walking a `curr` pointer and appending until it becomes None would be clearer. The `for` loop also re-assigns `head.next = None` through that trick rather than stating it explicitly, which makes the termination invariant harder to see.
complexity.summary: Collects all nodes into an array (with a trailing None sentinel), then walks the array rewiring each node's next pointer to its predecessor, returning the former tail as the new head.
